phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now in this problem, a person is standing at a window which is ten meter above the ground.
From that window,
the angle of elevation to the top of the tower
is thirty degrees,
and the angle of depression to the foot of the tower
is forty-five degrees.
What do we need to find?
We need to find the total height of the tower.
A small diagram will make this very easy.
Draw the window ten meter above the ground.
From the window,
draw a line going down to the foot of the tower.
This makes an angle of depression of forty-five degrees.
Also, draw a line going up to the top of the tower.
This makes an angle of elevation of
thirty degrees.
Let the horizontal distance between the building and the tower be x.
First,
let us use the forty-five degree angle.
For the triangle formed with the foot of the tower,
tan forty-five degree equal to opposite side upon adjacent side here. The opposite side is equal to the height of window, which is ten meters,
and the adjacent side is x.
So one equals ten over x. This gives x equals ten meters.
Got it?
Perfect.
We have found the distance between the building and the tower. Now that we know the distance, we can use it to find the extra height of the tower
above the window level. Let that extra height be h.
Now for the thirty degree triangle, tan thirty degrees equals h upon ten.
We know that tan thirty degrees is equal to one upon root three,
so one upon root three is equal to h upon ten. After solving this, we get h equals ten upon root three meters.
Done.
But be very sure about one thing.
This is not the total height of the tower.
This is only the part of the tower
which is above the window.
The window itself is already ten meters above the ground,
so total tower height
becomes ten plus ten upon root three meters.
Hence,
the final answer will be ten plus ten
divided by the square root of three meters.
So the correct option is option A.
